options.text: A static image showing only one isolated screen
options.misconception: cannot show the navigation between different screens

options.text: A written description listing the planned features
options.misconception: does not allow users to actually interact with anything

questions.hint: What lets users try a design before it is fully built?

questions.learningObjective: evaluate accessible design in a design critique
questions.stem: On Accessible design: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that an interface conveys meaning only through color and very small icons. What is the main accessibility concern here?

options.text: Not all users are able to perceive color or tiny details
All users have exactly the same visual abilities and needs
options.misconception: denies the broad range of human abilities

options.text: Accessibility applies exclusively to printed paper materials
options.misconception: narrows the scope of accessibility incorrectly

options.text: Color is never a valid design tool under any circumstances
options.misconception: overstates the restriction that accessibility implies

questions.explanation: Inclusive design accounts for varied abilities, including differences in color vision and visual acuity. Conveying meaning through color or tiny icons alone excludes some users, so redundant cues and sufficient size improve access.

questions.stem: Regarding Accessible design: a designer reviewing a conference name badge notices that an interface conveys meaning only through color and very small icons. What is the main accessibility concern here?

options.text: All users have exactly the same visual abilities and needs
options.misconception: denies the broad range of human abilities

options.text: Not all users are able to perceive color or tiny details
Accessibility applies exclusively to printed paper materials
options.misconception: narrows the scope of accessibility incorrectly

options.text: Color is never a valid design tool under any circumstances
options.misconception: overstates the restriction that accessibility implies

questions.explanation: Inclusive design accounts for varied abilities, including differences in color vision and visual acuity. Conveying meaning through color or tiny icons alone excludes some users, so redundant cues and sufficient size improve access.
questions.hint: Who might be left out if color is the only cue carrying meaning?
